brief: The Calloway farm. Crew 4 is digging FORGE’s old wrecks out of their own wheat.
Meet Rook at the barn, then guard the dig. The Wraith is the only mech Crew 4 has.

0: ROOK
Wraith, this is Rook. I’m parked by the barn. Walk on over.
ROOK
Left thumb walks, right thumb aims. Tap JET to hop, hold it to hover.
1: Rook! Something just twitched in the wreck pile.
Scrap doesn’t twitch. Wraith, get in the ring and hold.
2: Three masts. The marker shows the nearest. Keep firing till it falls.

panels.picture: Dawn over a sea of gold wheat studded with half-buried 2126 war machines: a tank tread with wheat growing through it, and in the distance a small white farmhouse leaning against the giant fallen claw of a harvester machine. In the middle band, a dig camp: tarps strung between the ribs of a dead Gunner, blue brine barrels breathing cold blue steam, one red-glass core glowing in a sling, a crew flag on a tall whip pole, and two tiny figures (a broad woman and a boy) at the barrels. Low sun from the left throws long shadows; the bottom third is wheat in deep shade.
lines: 2176. For fifty years FORGE’s war zones were fenced off. Now the fence is down, and the rush is on.
Every dead machine out there holds a core of red glass, still warm. One core heats a farmhouse all winter.
Live ones bite. Dunk them in brine till they hiss and go grey. Then they’re safe.
Red eye, run! Grey eye, done!

panels.picture: Morning in the Calloway yard: the small farmhouse leans against a huge fallen harvester claw, and beside it kneels the Wraith, a 6.6 m orange-and-charcoal mech with white stripes and amber lights, a freshly painted white wolf’s head still wet on its shoulder. A boy of twelve stands at the top of a tall ladder against the shoulder with a paint can, a big grey-haired woman with cutting goggles pushed up on her forehead stands below with her arms folded, and Jo, in the orange helmet, sits on the rim of the open cockpit hatch, all three small against the machine. Warm low sun from behind the house; the bottom third is the shadowed dirt yard.
lines: Wolves are done, Jo! Same wolves Howl had when he broke FORGE. Now it looks like a real war mech.
It’s a survey mech, Pip. Right, Gran?
Not today. The co-op’s sending a handler out. Calls herself Rook.
Bet she’s never seen wolves like these.

panels.picture: The edge of the dig at noon: small smoking drone wrecks lie in the trampled wheat around the Wraith’s feet, and Crew 4’s people crouch small behind blue brine barrels, one holding up a crackling handheld radio. On the low ridge behind stand three tall lattice relay masts, a red lamp pulsing at each top, and in the wreck pile below them every old machine’s red eye has turned toward the masts. Hard, flat noon light; the bottom third is calm trampled wheat.
lines: Look at the wrecks. Every eye’s turned to the masts on the ridge. Somebody’s talking to them.
Crew 4. This field is claimed. Leave it.
Claimed? My dad was born in that field.

panels.picture: Late golden afternoon by a weathered barn: out in the wheat the three relay masts lie toppled, their red lamps dark. In the middle band Rook leans on the open door of her battered orange crane truck: small and wiry, cropped white hair, an oilskin coat, a taped old army headset round her neck. She looks up at the Wraith, where Jo, in the orange helmet, sits in the open hatch; blue steam drifts off the brine barrels, and the bottom third is the barn’s long shadow.
lines: Masts are down. Not bad shooting, Wraith.
I’m a spotter, Rook. I find things. I don’t usually blow them up.
Then find me whoever was talking through them. Bring it home, Wraith.
Bring what home? I’m standing in my own yard.

brief: Harbor 9 at midnight: the boom town where every dig crew sells its cores.
Somebody planted spawner pods in the container stacks overnight. Find all four.

0: ROOK
Stick to the lanes. Those stacks are too tall to hop, even for you.
1: Pods print Skitters till you break them. The marker shows the nearest.
Those crates came off claimed ground.
2: Gunner on the quay! Get under the middle crane. I’m lifting you out.

panels.picture: Harbor 9 at midnight, seen from the quay: giant dock cranes and towering container stacks under hard sodium lamps, and dig crews wheeling crates of glowing red cores and dull grey ones past a big chalk price board whose writing is a blur. In the middle band, under one white floodlight on a loading platform, a tall man in a long bone-white coat with one white glove stands small against a wall of clean white containers; the Wraith waits at the quay’s edge with its amber lights on. The bottom third is dark wet concrete and black water.
lines: Our crates sail on the morning boat. That’s a new barn roof, right there.
A Gunner core’s worth three hundred! What’s “LIVE: ASK AT VANE” mean?
A red core nobody quenched. Selling those is against the law. Silas Vane pays triple anyway.
Man in the white coat. If he calls you friend, count your fingers.

panels.picture: A narrow container lane at night: in the middle band a split-open wooden farm crate spills dull grey cores across the concrete, and wedged inside it is the burst black husk of a spawner pod, still glowing red along its seams. Across the lane, neat stacks of clean bone-white containers stand untouched under a hard white floodlight. One orange-and-charcoal leg of the Wraith stands at the left edge, its amber light falling on the crate; the bottom third is wet dark concrete.
lines: Rook. All four pods were hidden in farm crates. Ours. Crew 2’s. Crew 6’s.
Right across the lane. Not one pod. Not a scratch.
Scare the farm crews off, then buy our fields cheap. That’s Vane all over.
Maybe. Vane’s a crook, but he’s a careful one.

panels.picture: Low angle from the quay: the Wraith hangs from the hook of a giant dock crane high above black water, amber lights glowing, harbor lamps smeared in the ripples, and Rook is a tiny silhouette in the lit crane cab. On the quay in the middle band, a tall man in a long bone-white coat looks up and lifts one white-gloved hand in a polite wave, his clean white containers behind him, and Bess, big with goggles pushed up, stands at the quay’s edge with her arms folded. Cold night light with one warm lamp on him; the bottom third is the dark quay edge and water.
lines: Lovely lift, Rook. Shame about all those farm crates, friend.
When Crew 4 gets tired of digging, I’ll buy that field. Fair price.
Fair like the place across the creek? Your diggers flattened that house in a day.
Old houses come down, Mrs. Calloway. Goodnight, friends.
Silas. You’re standing under my hook.

brief: Crew 7 has gone quiet in the pine woods, out by a field of 2126 wrecks.
Find them, guard Rook while she loads them up, and watch the trees for the pack.

0: ROOK
Their beacon’s east of the trail. Watch the trees.
ROOK
Hounds crouch, then charge dead straight. Sidestep or hop.
1: Found them. All three alive, and grumpy. Give me one minute to load up.
Keep them off my truck, Wraith. Stay in the ring.
2: Eyes up. Rust-red one coming out of the trees, twice the size.
Clear its pack first, then keep moving. It charges harder.
3: Crew 7’s clear. Meet me up on the north ridge.

panels.picture: Morning in the pine woods: pines taller than a war machine grow up through mossy 2126 wrecks, with shafts of sunlight slanting between the trunks. On the dirt trail in the middle band, Rook’s battered orange crane truck has stopped; Rook, small in her oilskin coat, stands on the running board pointing into the trees, and the Wraith stands beside the truck with its head among the lowest branches. Far off between the trunks a crew flag hangs limp on a whip pole beside a small blinking white beacon; the bottom third is ferns in shadow.
lines: The pine woods burned in the war. Now they stand taller than a Gunner, and the wrecks wear moss.
No word from Crew 7 since sunup. A dad and two kids, digging by the old wreck field.
Shouldn’t you wait back at the road?
In 2126 I sat in a bunker and listened. I’m done sitting.

panels.picture: A small clearing among giant pines: Crew 7, a father and two kids wrapped in grey blankets, sit among their crates in the back of Rook’s orange truck. Rook stands frozen beside the cab, one hand pressing the old taped headset to her ear, staring at nothing, with the Wraith looming behind her. Deep in the dark trees, pairs of red eyes watch; the light is dim green-gold through the canopy, and the bottom third is shadowed ferns.
lines: Get your crew out of my yards, Birdie.
Rook doesn’t answer. For a long moment, she doesn’t move.
Nobody’s called me that in fifty years.

panels.picture: Sunset on a bare ridge above the pines: Rook’s orange crane truck is parked with the huge rust-red head and shoulders of the Alpha Hound hanging from its hook, horns and spine blades dark, eyes out. Rook, small, stands on the truck bed shining a torch on a seam of bright silver welds that stand out against the rust, and the Wraith stands behind with Jo, in the orange helmet, leaning out of the hatch. Warm low sun from behind; the bottom third is dark ridge grass.
lines: Look at these welds instead. Bright. Clean. This thing was built this year.
FORGE is dead. So who’s building new ones?
Did you get the big one? I’m calling it Biscuit!
We are not calling it Biscuit.

brief: Night fog on the creek road. Rook is driving Crew 7 and their cores out of the woods.
Escort her truck to the south road. If the truck is destroyed, the mission fails.

0: ROOK
I only roll while you’re close, Wraith. Stay within 35 metres.
ROOK
Some of them go for my truck. Kill those first.
UNKNOWN
Leave the cores on the road and walk home.

panels.picture: Night fog along a creek road through tall pines: Rook’s battered orange crane truck stands with its headlights cutting two beams into the mist, its bed stacked with crates and blue brine barrels breathing cold steam. The Wraith stands alongside with its amber lights glowing; Rook leans out of the driver’s window looking up at it, and a small kid in a blanket peers out of the passenger side. The soft glow of the fog is the only light; the bottom third is dark wet road.
lines: Miss Rook? What’s the pilot’s real name?

panels.picture: Inside Rook’s truck cab at night: amber dashboard light and a fogged windscreen, through which the Wraith’s lights glow in the mist with red machine eyes beyond. Tucked into the dashboard frame in the middle band is a faded old photograph of a young pilot standing by a tall mech with a white wolf on its shoulder; a kid in a blanket leans forward pointing at it, and Rook’s weathered hands grip the wheel. Warm dash glow against cold blue fog; the bottom third is the dark dashboard.
lines: Who’s the man in the photo? His mech’s got wolves on it. Like yours.
Howl. My pilot. He never came out of Foundry 4.
My kid brother copied our wolves off an old poster of him.

panels.picture: Dawn at the edge of the woods: fog lifting off a gravel road, pale gold light behind the pines. Rook’s orange truck has stopped; Rook sits on the tailgate with a steaming tin cup while Crew 7’s dad lifts his two kids down beside her, and the Wraith kneels at the roadside with Jo, in the orange helmet, sitting in the open hatch. Soft early light; the bottom third is the quiet road in shadow.
lines: That’s four fights now. Nobody’s been hurt. Not once.
I noticed. They chase folks off, they take the cores, and they let everyone walk.

brief: A storm over the farm fields. The voice reaches its machines through three relays.
Take all three relays: hold each ring until it’s full. Then Rook can trace the signal.

0: ROOK
Stand in each ring till it fills. Never mind the lightning. It only hits them.
UNKNOWN
Copy, Wraith. Trace all you like. Then go home.
1: Something huge on the east road. Bone white. Use cover between bursts.

panels.picture: Night storm over the wheat: lightning splits the sky and lights three distant relay towers standing in the field. In the middle band a line of dig-crew trucks drives away, their crew flags torn and whipping, while Rook’s orange truck is parked facing the other way with a laptop glowing in its cab, and the Wraith stands beside it in the rain with its amber lights on. Cold flash light; the bottom third is dark, wind-flattened wheat.
lines: A storm rolls over farm country. Three more crews have packed up and left this week.
Crew 2 sold their claim to Vane this morning. For next to nothing.
Then we find the voice before anyone else sells. It talks through relays. Relays can be traced.
So I stand in the lightning while you sit in the truck.
I’m seventy-four, Wraith. Everything on me is out of warranty. I get the truck.

panels.picture: Inside Rook’s truck cab in the storm: rain streams down the windscreen, and on the dash a battered laptop shows a dark map with one bright line running straight across it to a small factory symbol. Rook’s lined face is lit by the screen, her taped headset on; through the glass, lightning shows the Wraith standing in a glowing ring in the wheat. The screen is the one strong light; the bottom third is the dark dashboard.
lines: Got it. The signal runs straight back to one place. Foundry 4.
Where Howl broke FORGE? That place has been cold since the war.

panels.picture: Grey dawn after the storm: the huge bone-white Gunner Prime lies face down in flattened wet wheat, steam rising off its armour, both arm cannons sprawled. The Wraith stands over it, rain-dark; at the field’s edge three tiny figures stand by Rook’s orange truck looking at the fallen machine: Rook in her oilskin coat, Bess (big, goggles pushed up) and Pip (a boy of twelve). Pale light breaks through the clouds; the bottom third is wet wheat in shadow.
lines: That’s three big ones down! I’m calling this one Marshmallow.
We are still not doing names.
Get some sleep, all of you. Tomorrow we drive to Foundry 4.
Rook. You don’t have to be the one who goes.
Fifty years I’ve stayed away from that gate, Bess. That’s long enough.

brief: The signal leads to Foundry 4: FORGE’s old heart, fenced off and cold since 2126.
Its furnaces are lit again. Hold the yard while Rook pulls the factory log.

0: ROOK
Furnaces are hot. Somebody’s been building in here.
1: Ninety seconds to pull the log. Hold the yard, Wraith.
Turn around. There’s nothing left in here for you.
2: Two big ones at the gate. Fine, Pip. Biscuit and Marshmallow.
3: Gate’s clear! Bring it home, Wraith. I’m right behind you.
Don’t you dare stop for me.

panels.picture: Night at the huge scarred gate of Foundry 4: beyond it, chimneys pour smoke lit red from below, and far back a tall tower holds a giant round eye. In the middle band, beside the gate, stands a small weathered bronze plaque on a post, its letters worn smooth; Rook, small, stands before it with a torch, her truck’s headlights behind her and the Wraith kneeling at her back. Red furnace glow on the clouds is the one strong light; the bottom third is dark cracked concrete.
lines: A plaque by the gate: UNITS 01–07 · 2126 · THEY HELD THE LINE.
Seven pilots. I learned every one of their names.
Eyes front, Wraith. Let’s go knock.

panels.picture: Deep in the foundry yard by furnace light: at the foot of the eye tower, a long hollow pressed into black slag shows the shape of a fallen mech, but it is empty, and two deep drag marks run out of it into the dark. Rook, small, stands at its edge pointing her torch down; the Wraith stands beside her with its amber lights on the slag. Red-orange furnace light from one side; the bottom third is dark slag.
lines: Got the log. Wraith… look down. By your left foot.
A hollow in the slag, the shape of a fallen mech. It’s empty. Drag marks lead off into the dark.
Howl’s mech went down right here. I said go, and he went.
We left him lying here. Somebody moved him.

panels.picture: Outside the gate at night, Rook sits sideways in her truck’s lit cab with the door open, holding up her battered laptop, the log on its screen; one small mark stands out on it, a seven lying on its side like a cattle brand. The Wraith stands guard behind the truck with its amber lights on, and through the gate the foundry chimneys glow red. Warm cab light against the red night; the bottom third is shadowed ground.
lines: The log names no one. Just orders. Hounds, Gunners, things I’ve never seen.
Every order’s signed with the same mark. A seven, lying on its side.

panels.picture: Looking back through the gate at the eye tower: FORGE’s huge round eye, cracked in a star, its cracks stitched together with bright new cables, flickering red. Far below, Rook and the Wraith stand tiny in the gateway, looking up. The eye’s red glow is the one strong light; the bottom third is the dark yard and gate.
lines: Look at the eye. The crack’s been stitched with new cable.
It flickers red. One more line crawls across Rook’s screen, older than the rest. No mark.
THE FIELDS BELONG TO THE FACTORY.
